title: BackendV1Call
description: One call to an EKKA backend adapter (`ekka.backend` v1) as the adapter receives it on its Unix socket: the operation, the path values its route names, the three required headers and the strict body. The route for each operation is in operations.json. The answer is `$defs.result`. The adapter verifies the Govern-signed gate token in `x-ekka-gate-token` offline before it reads anything else, enforces the limits the token carries (governance/grant-constraints), and never answers with a backend's own error text. Nothing in this contract names a backend's API: the adapter's driver turns each operation into its backend's calls.

name.description: The `{name}` value of the route: the desk's name.

provider.description: The `{provider}` value of the route: a provider's name.

operation.description: Eight operations, and `provider_connect`, which is reserved: it is part of the vocabulary and answers refused, code NOT_AVAILABLE, in v1.

resource_version.description: The backend's version of a desk's configuration, as the adapter last read it. A change that names one is applied only if the desk is still at that version, so two admins never overwrite each other.

headers.description: Header names in lowercase, as HTTP compares them. The API gate adds all four on every call to the adapter, and a plan cannot set any of them.

x-ekka-gate-token.description: Base64 of the Govern-signed gate token (governance/gate-token.schema.json) for exactly this call: organization, API-gate instance, resource `apis/desks`, operation and expiry. Its `scope.contract` is `ekka.gate.api.v1`, the API gate's contract that Govern signs; the backend protocol is never in the token, it is `x-ekka-backend-contract`. The grant's limits are under `constraints.grant`, checked against governance/grant-constraints/desks.v1.schema.json; `constraints.body_sha256` beside it pins this call's body. Verified offline against Govern's published `gate_token` key. Never logged.

authorization.description: The backend's administration credential, placed by the organization in the Enclave's vault and injected by the API gate on each call. The adapter keeps no credential at rest. Never logged.

x-ekka-operation-id.description: `<run id>/<step id>/<task id>`: the fully qualified execution identity. Govern mints a fresh task id for every execution of an operation, so two operations that each hold a step with the same id, a new visit of a looping operation and a workflow retry all get distinct ids, while a redelivery of the same task keeps its id. The adapter records it with a digest of the request before it calls the backend: the same id with the same request answers the recorded outcome with `delivery: duplicate`, and the same id with a different request is refused OPERATION_ID_REUSED. Its run id must equal the token's.

x-ekka-backend-contract.description: The backend protocol this call speaks. Read from this header, never from the token. An adapter refuses a call naming a protocol it does not serve.

image.description: The image by digest, never a tag, in one of two forms. `<name>@sha256:<64 hex>`: an image from a registry, by its registry digest. `sha256:<64 hex>` alone: an image the machine built itself, by its local content ID (Docker's image ID, `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}'`), which the backend uses as it is and never pulls. The two are different hashes of one image, so a registry digest never matches a content ID. The digest (after `@`, or the whole value) must be in the limits' `image_digests`; hex is lowercase and exactly 64 characters.

policy.description: The desk's starting network policy, in the backend's own form, which the adapter's driver reads. Its digest, computed by the adapter, must be in the limits' `policy_digests`, and every host it allows must be inside `allowed_hosts`.

providers.description: Providers to attach, each in the limits' `providers`, with its configuration matching `provider_config_digests`.

environment.description: Plain environment values. Each name must be in the limits' `environment_keys`. Never a secret: a provider carries secrets.

repo.description: Not used, and kept only so an older caller's empty value is not refused. A repository reaches a desk through a setup plan run on the desk, never through create. A non-empty value is refused FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED; absent or empty is the same.

policy.description: The whole resulting policy, in the backend's own form. Every host it allows must be inside the limits' `allowed_hosts`.

code.description: Why an answer is refused, or what is not known. A CONSTRAINT_ code names the limit that refused it. Our own words only: a backend's error text is never forwarded. DESK_BUSY: the desk is held by a running job or another change; nothing changed, and the change may be asked again once the desk is free. CONSTRAINT_CREDENTIAL_ENDPOINT: a policy change would add, change or move a network endpoint that carries a provider's credentials; it has no limit of its own, because changing where a provider's credentials reach is a provider change, made at install, never a policy change. NOT_APPLIED: the create never reached the desk; nothing was created.

result.description: Every answer is in this closed shape. `ready`, `refused` and `unknown` are sent with HTTP 200; `running` is sent with HTTP 202, and only when a change reaches the adapter's deadline. Both are 2xx, so the API gate reads the facts either way; a step's facts come only from a 2xx answer, by field name. The fact a plan reads is `outcome` itself, declared with enum `ready|refused|unknown`, and `desk_ready`. The enum leaves out `running` on purpose: a 202 fails the plan's fact check on arrival and the step fails closed. `delivery` says whether this answer is new or recorded, so a refusal delivered twice stays refused. `desk_ready` is written from `outcome` by the table in operations.json, and this schema refuses an answer that disagrees with it.

delivery.description: `first`: this call did the work. `duplicate`: this operation id was already answered, and this is the recorded answer; nothing was sent to the backend again.

outcome.description: `ready`: done, and the desk is ready. `refused`: nothing changed; `code` says why. `unknown`: the change completed or stopped (a settle marker proved it), but the resulting desk does not match the request; a person checks before any retry. `running`: the change reached the adapter's deadline and is not finished; only ever an HTTP 202, carrying `operation_id`. The next `status` of that desk reconciles it.

backend_id.description: The backend's id for the desk. It stays on the customer's machine: a plan declares no fact for it.

providers_digest.description: On `status`: EKKA's digest of the desk's providers, computed by the adapter over the gateway's provider records, so the Enclave can re-pin after a governed disconnect.

operation_id.description: On `running` only: the operation still in progress, as the adapter's request id for it, a lowercase hyphenated UUID. It is the id the desk's lock names and the id `ekka desk release --operation` and `up.sh desks settle --operation` take; never the call's `X-EKKA-Operation-Id`, which is only the input.
